opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, but write was requested). Requested level is within policy, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E046 (Daniel Gutierrez): contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training means maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment status for E046 (Daniel Gutierrez). The HR note states full-time Payroll Specialist (max write), while the Security note states contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; basic training caps access at read. Because the Security record explicitly identifies E046 as a contractor with basic training, granting write would exceed the maximum allowed. Granting read complies with policy under both interpretations. Requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, so grant the maximum allowed: read.
